steps: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices through a transmission medium.
Its key components are: sender, receiver, message, transmission medium and protocol.
A protocol is a set of rules that governs communication between devices.
items.finalAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between devices; its components are sender, receiver, message, transmission medium and protocol.

steps: A router connects two or more different networks.
It examines the destination IP address of a packet and forwards the packet towards its destination.
A router selects an appropriate path for sending data between networks.
items.finalAnswer: A router connects networks and forwards packets towards their destinations using IP addresses.

steps: The Network Layer provides logical addressing, such as IP addresses, to identify devices on a network.
It determines routes and forwards packets from the source network to the destination network.
It may divide packets into smaller units and reassemble them at the destination.
items.finalAnswer: The Network Layer provides logical addressing, routing and packet forwarding between networks.

steps: In circuit switching, a dedicated communication path is established between the sender and receiver before data is sent.
The dedicated path remains reserved for the duration of the communication.
In packet switching, data is divided into packets that may travel through different paths to the destination.
Packets are reassembled at the destination; network resources are shared among users.
items.finalAnswer: Circuit switching reserves a dedicated path, whereas packet switching sends data in packets over shared network paths.

steps: DHCP stands for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
It automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining a network.
It can also provide other network settings, such as the subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server address.
items.finalAnswer: DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses and other network settings to devices.

steps: Encapsulation is the process of adding protocol information, such as headers, to data as it moves down the network layers.
The receiving device removes these headers as the data moves up the layers; this process is called decapsulation.
Encapsulation organises data for transmission, but it does not by itself make communication secure.
Encryption is used to protect data from being read by unauthorised users.
items.finalAnswer: Encapsulation prepares data for transmission but does not itself provide security; encryption protects data from unauthorised reading.

steps: TCP is a reliable, connection-oriented protocol.
It checks that data is delivered in order and uses acknowledgements and retransmissions to recover lost data.
UDP is a connectionless protocol and does not guarantee delivery, order or retransmission of lost data.
UDP has less overhead and is generally faster than TCP.
items.finalAnswer: TCP provides reliable, ordered data transfer, while UDP does not guarantee delivery or order.

steps: Encryption converts readable data (plaintext) into an unreadable form (ciphertext) using an encryption key.
Only a user with the correct decryption key can convert the ciphertext back into readable data.
Encryption helps prevent unauthorised users from understanding data sent over a network.
items.finalAnswer: Encryption protects network data by making it unreadable to unauthorised users.
